messages:
lina.support: Hey team — Brightline reported a sudden embeddings throughput drop starting ~03:30 UTC. Tokens/sec for their traffic is steady but vectors/sec fell ~60%, latencies up, queuing observed. No auth errors. Customer says they didn't change client schema.

mike.eng: Thanks — do we have a repro? Any errors in the gateway or worker logs?

lina.support: I asked for logs; they attached a short run: `POST /v1/embeddings` of ~1k small docs, payload shows `model: embed-redwood-1536`, `batch_size: auto`. They see many requests piling in the queue and backend `429` from internal router occasionally.

juan-ml: Quick sanity check: tokens/sec stable => generator path fine, embedding path throttled. Could be batching/window change, or kvcache/contention. Any recent rollout to embedding handler?

mike.eng: I dug into deploys — there was a config rollout 03:00 UTC that adjusted `batch_window_ms` heuristics for embeddings to favor latency (shorter window) for small requests. That should reduce batching, not increase queueing. Strange.

lina.support: Attaching their minimal repro curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"embed-redwood-1536","input":["short text..." for i in range(1000)]}'``` They said switching to `embed-redwood-512` temporarily returns to normal throughput.

juan-ml: Hmm model variant change helps — suggests model-specific perf regression or memory/KV cache pressure for 1536 variant. Any GPU saturation on hosts serving 1536?

mike.eng: I pulled `nvidia-smi` and worker metrics for the mid-03:00 window: GPU util bounced high intermittently; we also see long GPU compute queues and growing `gpu_kv_cache_size` metrics. Snippet from time-series: `gpu_queue_depth: 82 -> 300` around 03:28.

ashley.ops: Also seeing autoscaler throttle events — Dedicated pool clipped new workers because of a per-tenant quota; a backlog formed while autoscaler tried to spin. Could be capacity/backoff interaction.

lina.support: Customer billing wasn't impacted, but they saw `429` from router while waiting. They flagged SLA breach.

mike.eng: Repro plan: I will run internal loadgen against embed-redwood-1536 with same request shape and `batch_window_ms` toggles. Also try forcing `prefer_variant=smaller` to see if routing helps.

juan-ml: Hypothesis list: 1) 1536 variant introduced a kernel/path regression that increases per-token GPU time (affects vectors/sec but not tokens/sec for text gen). 2) KV cache growth leads to slower KV lookups and GPU stalls when batch sizes vary. 3) Autoscaler/quota interplay created queuing until new hosts accepted traffic.

mike.eng: Quick mitigation I'm suggesting to ops: add temporary routing weight to 512 variant for Brightline's key and increase autoscaler burst limit for the affected pool. That should reduce queue depth while we debug.

ashley.ops: Done: bumped burst and routed ~40% of their traffic to embed-redwood-512 at 03:45. Queue depth dropped to ~30, vectors/sec improved to ~85% of baseline per quick check. Customer confirmed partial recovery. :thumbsup:

lina.support: Customer acknowledged improvement but requests full RCA. They're asking for repro steps and timeline.

mike.eng: Repro notes (quick): run `loadgen_embeddings.py --model embed-redwood-1536 --clients 100 --rps 1200 --size small` — compare vectors/sec and ``gpu_queue_depth``. I also captured a pair of server traces showing longer kernel launch latency for the 1536 path: ```[03:27:12] kernel_launch_ms: 2.3, [03:28:01] kernel_launch_ms: 9.8, compute_ms: 120 -> 340```

juan-ml: I'll pull the model build parameters and recent quantization/conv kernel changes. If a recent fused-kernel landed for 1536, it might be blocking multi-batch efficiency.

mike.eng: Also found a pattern in router logs: when batch-size variance spikes (many 1-2 item requests mixed with occasional 64-item requests), our batching code falls back to conservative path causing more GPU launches per token. That combined with KV cache thrash and autoscaler backlog explains the sawtooth vectors/sec.

lina.support: Customer asked if dimension mismatch could cause this — they confirm vector dim matches expected 1536. No mismatch.

mike.eng: Next steps: (1) Juan to verify kernel/regression and revert if found. (2) I will add a temporary heuristics tweak to avoid fallback path when we detect high variance workloads. (3) Ops keep 40% routed to 512 for Brightline until resolved. (4) Lina to send customer a timeline and mitigations.

juan-ml: I'll prioritize kernel diff and post findings in this thread. If it's not kernel, I'll instrument KV lookups and GPU launch latency further.

ashley.ops: FYI — autoscaler logs show quota error at 03:25 for that pool: `quota_exceeded: tenant_burst_capacity`. I'm proposing an autoscaler policy change to prevent blocking in the middle of heavy bursts — will open a quick PR.

mike.eng: Recording action items in SRE: create incident ticket, attach loadgen config and traces. Lina please cc customer in incident follow-up.

lina.support: Will do. Customer wants daily updates until RCA. I'll post their repro artifacts and links to the traces.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-8345. Assigned: eng-runtime (mike.eng), eng-ml (juan-ml), ops (ashley.ops). Priority: P2.
